clue.text: Was he angry when accepting this award?

definitions.text: Was he angry when accepting this award?

parts.words: Was he angry when accepting this award?
parts.note: a man called George who is cross would be the recipient of a British gallantry medal named for a king

explanation.surface: A question about whether a prizewinner was annoyed at the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the medal's name as a sentence: a man named George who is angry. The award itself is a British decoration for civilian bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: This British civilian gallantry decoration was instituted by King George VI in 1940.

clue.text: Noted composition for spirited duet with energy

indicators.note: lively or spirited suggests the letters of the word duet dance into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A musical piece is written for an energetic pair of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirited' rearranges DUET into ETUD, then E for energy finishes it. 'Noted' means set in musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A study piece for an instrument is a short musical work written down in notes.

clue.text: Feeling of guilt concerning the code

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
Morse is the famous telegraphic code of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Someone feels guilty about breaking a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrition is the regretful feeling of having done wrong.

clue.text: Recruit an engineer with lots of time available

parts.note: an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: A firm hires an engineer who has plenty of free time.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire or take on someone for work is to recruit them.

clue.text: Out of control nato riot caused a revolution

indicators.note: things out of control run wild, so the letters of nato riot are scrambled

explanation.surface: A riot by NATO troops that got out of hand toppled the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' rearranges NATO RIOT. 'revolution' looks political but means a turning.
explanation.definitionFit: A single turn of a wheel about its axis is one revolution, a spinning movement.

clue.text: Beat a runner

definitions.meaning: to strike a child with a soft shoe, as a punishment in old schools
one that slips, or a skid or runner fitted under a wheel or sledge

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names soft indoor footwear used for spanking and also a slipping skid, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Can only go forwards when you have this

definitions.text: Can only go forwards when you have this

parts.words: Can only go forwards when you have this
parts.note: someone pressed against a barrier behind cannot retreat, which is the idiom for being in a desperate position

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what forces you onward and never back.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally, with a wall behind you, the only way to move is forward; the idiom means being cornered.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being cornered with no escape route, so pressing on is the sole option.

clue.text: Get hog to gnaw the shell using this

definitions.text: Get hog to gnaw the shell using this

indicators.note: gnawing chews something up, so the letters of get hog to are mangled

explanation.surface: Advice on making a pig chew through a shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnaw' rearranges GET HOG TO. The whole clue also describes the little point a hatching chick uses to chip through its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatchling birds and reptiles have a tiny hard tip on the beak or snout for breaking out of the egg.

clue.text: Extra

parts.note: a film extra is a background performer, an anonymous member of a mass scene

explanation.definitionFit: A film extra plays an anonymous face in a mass scene, an ordinary member of the public.

clue.text: Fish for some ray under water

indicators.note: only some of the letters of ray under water are taken, a run from inside them

explanation.surface: Fishing for a ray in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks letters from inside 'ray under'. The answer is a small sweetfish of Japan and China.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweetfish is a small East Asian freshwater species prized as food.

clue.text: Embarking the elderly

definitions.meaning: advancing in years, said of older people

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both boarding a vehicle and growing old.

clue.text: Driving instruction at Calais, perhaps

parts.note: British drivers arriving in France must switch to driving on the opposite side of the road from home

explanation.surface: A road sign seen on landing in a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain drives on the left; France, entered at the port of Calais, drives on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a road-sign command telling motorists which side of the carriageway to stay on.

clue.text: Irishman expressing joy over garden area

indicators.note: in this across clue over places the name before the cry of joy

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is the stock Irishman of crosswords
io is an old cry of triumph or joy

explanation.surface: An Irishman is delighted with his garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor space beside a house is used for sitting and eating.

clue.text: Soundly study the plant

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so the word for study is heard as a homophone

parts.note: to read is to study, as in reading law at university

explanation.surface: A botanist examines a plant thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall grass of marshes and riverbanks with hollow stems.

clue.text: Denying a silly yearning

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of yearning are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit a foolish longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges YEARNING. The answer is an archaic word for refusing or disowning.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for refusing or disowning, from Middle English, means saying no.

clue.text: Do stop or crash into the jamb

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters of do stop or are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A warning to a driver about to hit the side of a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright side post of a doorframe is called a jamb.

clue.text: Endorsed as a fine, resolute pressman

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
firm means steadfast and resolute
ed, short for editor, is a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A determined journalist backs something after paying a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm or approve formally is to endorse.

clue.text: Restrain worker by the sleeve

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
the cuff is the end part of a sleeve

explanation.surface: Grabbing a labourer by his sleeve to hold him back.
explanation.definitionFit: To shackle someone's wrists is to restrain them.

clue.text: Brave about carpet burn

indicators.note: about means around, so the Native American people go round the floor covering

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the Cree are a Native American people
a mat is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A bold person deals with a rug that got scorched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun, a Native American warrior, here exemplified by the CREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce a corpse to ashes by fire is a solemn kind of burning.

clue.text: Club which finally provided a steam-room

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball

indicators.note: finally takes the end letter of the word which

explanation.surface: A sports club that, in the end, built a sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish bath is a steam-room for sweating and washing.

clue.text: Facing a stag in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so the letters of a stag in are mixed up

explanation.surface: Confronting a deer that is in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning on or set opposite something means facing it, as in up against the wall.

clue.text: She joined Midlands sports centre then sustained a rupture

parts.note: her is the object form of she
the NIA was the National Indoor Arena in Birmingham, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A woman joined a gym in Birmingham and then got injured.
explanation.walkthrough: The NIA was Birmingham's National Indoor Arena, a sports venue in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical protrusion of an organ through the wall of a cavity is a tear or rupture.

clue.text: Wagon mentioned by John, for example

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the old word for a wagon is heard as a homophone

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A wagon referred to by someone named John.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a surname: John is an example of a person so named, the Western film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood cowboy actor was a famous bearer of this surname, first name John.

clue.text: I audibly defame someone from Reykjavik, probably

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the spoken phrase is a homophone

parts.note: to slander is to defame by spoken words

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to badmouthing a person from Iceland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Say I then SLANDER aloud ('audibly') and you hear the answer, the second word spelt CELANDER. 'probably' because not everyone in Reykjavik is a native.
explanation.definitionFit: Reykjavik is the capital of Iceland, so a resident there is likely a native of that island nation.

clue.text: Rush up to catch train starting to stop

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so the turned plant word holds the first letter
in a down clue up means the plant word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant

indicators.note: starting takes the opening letter of the word train

explanation.surface: Hurry upward to board a train just as it starts to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REED into DEER; 'to catch' puts the T of train ('starting') inside. 'Rush' is a plant, not a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage or prevent someone from acting is to stop them.

clue.text: Secure capital for European chief magistrate

parts.note: to land something is to secure it, as in landing a deal
Amman is the capital of Jordan

explanation.surface: Winning a capital city for Europe's top judge.
explanation.definitionFit: In several Swiss cantons the head of government and court is titled this way.

clue.text: Start the activities with a game of marbles

indicators.note: start takes the opening letter of each of the words the activities with

explanation.surface: Kick off the fun by playing marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' takes the first letters of 'the activities with'. The answer is a large shooting marble, or a marbles game.
explanation.definitionFit: This word names a large choice marble and also a game played with such marbles.

clue.text: Scholastic titles great artists held no doubt

definitions.text: Scholastic titles great artists held no doubt

parts.words: Scholastic titles great artists held no doubt
parts.note: the great painters were the leading old masters, so they would be the top masters, the titles of school principals

explanation.surface: The famous painters surely had academic job titles.
explanation.walkthrough: The greatest of the old masters would be the masters at the head, the title of school principals.
explanation.definitionFit: The principals in charge of schools hold these titles, from a master at the head.
